name: Harfang 3D
listed_description: 3D visualization library usable in C++, Python, Lua and Go. Based on BGFX
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The GitHub page (659 stars, LGPL-3.0 plus GPLv3 and commercial licensing, default branch main) and the README (readme.md) hold only qualitative claims ('Performance oriented', 'optimized'); the single number is that screenshots were captured on a 1080GTX at 1080p running at 60FPS, which compares nothing. It is built on bgfx, which supports Vulkan, Metal, DirectX 9-12, OpenGL and OpenGL ES, but no per-backend or OpenGL/DirectX timing is published. One WebSearch for Harfang versus Unity/Unreal performance found no benchmark mentioning Harfang. Guessed OpenGL/DirectX baseline does not apply (it is a layer over those APIs through bgfx).

name: herebedragons
listed_description: A basic 3D scene implemented with various engines, frameworks or APIs
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. It is a collection of 21 renderings of one scene (OpenGL, Vulkan, Metal, DX9/11/12, WebGL, WebGPU, Unity, Unreal, Godot, Cycles, a software renderer, consoles and others). The top README states the comparison is 'inherently biased' and gives no timings; all 21 per-API READMEs were fetched and searched for fps, ms, frame time, faster, slower and performance, and none has a frame time or FPS comparison (only 'running at 30 or 60 FPS' for the Dreamcast build and '25 or 50 FPS' for the PS2 build, each a mode of one build, not a comparison). Not a performance project; the guessed OpenGL/DirectX baseline gives no speed claim.

name: Horde3D
listed_description: A small 3D rendering and animation engine
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The GitHub page (1.6k stars, EPL-1.0) and README list features (occlusion culling, LOD, binary model format 'for maximum performance') with no benchmark or comparison; the only speed number is that Ninja builds up to two-three times faster than make, which is about compiling the project, not the engine. One WebSearch (Horde3D versus Ogre3D/Irrlicht fps) found only unrelated Irrlicht forum anecdotes, none with Horde3D numbers. horde3d.org and its wiki were not reachable. Guessed OpenGL/DirectX baseline does not apply (it is built on OpenGL).

name: ITK
listed_description: An open-source, cross-platform system for image analysis.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The listed page https://www.itk.org/ was not opened; the GitHub repo (1.7k stars, Apache-2.0) README makes no performance claim. Release notes 5.0, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4.0, 6.0b01 and 6.0b02 contain no 'faster than' comparison with another library. The companion ITKPerformanceBenchmarking repo is only a harness for timing ITK itself across versions and platforms (no results, no hardware); its Insight Journal paper (insight-journal.org/pdfs/972.pdf) and the ITK mailing-list threads on comparing against OpenCV were EGRESS_BLOCKED or ENOTFOUND. Two WebSearches (ITK versus OpenCV, scikit-image, SimpleITK timings) found no published cross-library benchmark; the mailing-list snippet advises benchmarking overlapping operations in release builds and says ITK is n-D and general while OpenCV is 2D and efficiency-focused.

name: LAME
listed_description: LAME is a high quality MPEG Audio Layer III (MP3) encoder.
reason: No numeric speed comparison in LAME's favor against any named baseline reachable. lame.sourceforge.io was not reachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND); the rbrito/lame GitHub mirror's README, USAGE, doc/html/index.html and 900 KB ChangeLog were read: the ChangeLog has only self-comparisons of its own versions (for example 'make VBR/ABR 1% faster', 'speed up of bin_search_stepsize ... 20% faster') and no other encoder is timed. Three WebSearches found: the 3.96/3.97 release notes (search snippet only) claim only 'Encodes faster than real time on a PII 266 at highest quality mode' (no named baseline) and quality parity with FhG; the Hydrogenaudio 128 kbps listening test (October 2008, snippet only, page blocked) says Fraunhofer and Helix 'outperform LAME in terms of encoding speed' (Helix at 90x), i.e. the evidence runs against LAME; a Phoronix/OpenBenchmarking LAME 3.100 (snippet only) WAV-to-MP3 test reports only LAME's own run times (Min 1 / Avg 1.73 / Max 12 minutes across systems). The project goal is quality, not speed; no recognizable baseline is beaten with numbers.
